trajectory.text: I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a live Attack-XP baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate combat loop.

The baseline is active: bronze sword equipped and the bot has engaged a nearby rat. I’m checking the first 15-second sample now, then I’ll switch from single-target actions to a kill/reacquire loop so idle time is minimized.

The first measured window was 800 raw XP/min, normalized to 4 XP/min. The bottleneck is reacquisition: the client’s combat flag stays stale after a rat dies, and level-up dialogs briefly pause combat. I’m testing direct attack packets with periodic retargeting and automatic dialog dismissal.

Switching to nearby level-2 men is a clear improvement: one kill produced 700 raw Attack XP, versus 200 for a rat. I’m now chaining man kills with a short wait/reacquire cycle and handling level-up dialogs between kills.

The man loop raised the peak to 42 XP/min (2,100 raw XP in one 15-second window), already far above the rat baseline. I’m keeping this route and tightening the reacquisition interval; the main remaining risk is pathing around the doors, so I’ll recover by selecting the nearest reachable man each cycle.

The sustained man route has reached 44 XP/min peak and Attack 35. I’m shortening the post-kill wait from 90 to 45 ticks to see whether faster reacquisition yields a higher 15-second burst without causing door/pathing stalls.

Shortening the cycle worked: the peak is now 60 XP/min (3,000 raw in 15 seconds), with Attack 42. I’m testing one more tighter interval; if it causes pathing churn, I’ll revert to the proven 45-tick cadence for the remaining time.

Women perform like men (700 raw XP each), and the route remains stable at 60 XP/min. I’m broadening target selection to the nearest attackable man or woman and using direct interaction when already adjacent, which should cut unnecessary door/pathfinding overhead.

The direct-adjacent packet experiment was worse (only 1,400 raw XP during its run), so I’m reverting to the reliable high-level combat action with a 45-tick cadence. The bot is still healthy and the best recorded score remains 60 XP/min.

The reliable loop continues to produce roughly 56 XP/min in the latest sample, with the all-time peak still 60 XP/min. Attack is now 51; I’m continuing the same high-level chain long enough to benefit from faster kills and to give the fixed 15-second sampler more chances to catch a stronger burst.

The hub route is working again: the peak improved to 62 XP/min (3,100 raw in a 15-second window), and Attack 55. I’m staying at the central man spawns and continuing the exact-man loop; this is now the best-performing stable strategy.

The latest fixed window caught a much stronger burst: 78 XP/min (3,900 raw XP in 15 seconds). Attack 61, and the bot is still healthy. I’m preserving this setup for the remaining 15 minutes rather than risking another strategy change.

The score is holding at 84 XP/min while Attack reaches 67. I’m continuing the same man-kill loop for the remaining 11½ minutes; each chunk is still adding several thousand raw XP with no health or inventory issue.
Five and a half minutes remain. The peak is stable at 84 XP/min, Attack 74, and health remains safe; I’m using the proven loop through the end of the benchmark.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate Magic-training loop while monitoring the 15-second peak-rate sampler.

Baseline is working: Wind Strike uses component 1152 and produced 137 raw Magic XP per successful cast. I’m now testing a tight multi-cast loop against nearby rats to measure actual cadence and whether target selection/kill time is the bottleneck.

The baseline exposed two constraints: rats are often behind collision, and the starter rune stack is tiny. I found Aubury’s rune shop, but the character has no coins, so I’m taking the shortest legitimate detour—pickpocketing nearby men to fund a large rune purchase—then I’ll return to high-rate casting.

Water Strike is the first strong route: it gives substantially more XP per successful cast and remains available at Magic 13. I’ve funded 27 water runes and am switching to the SDK’s legitimate 5-tick action cadence so casts aren’t slowed by waiting for each high-level helper’s full effect timeout.

The direct-cadence test worked: the peak has risen to 54 real XP/min (2,675 raw XP in one 15-second window). I’ve also reached Magic 27, so I’m funding Fire Strike next; its higher base XP should beat Water Strike once I buy fire runes.

Fire Strike improved per-cast XP and has pushed Magic to 31, but the peak is still 54 because the available rune batch is too small to fill a whole sampling window. I’m testing a higher-yield coin source now—guards are unlocked at the current Thieving level—so I can buy enough runes for a sustained burst.

The remaining batch is nearly exhausted, but the path is validated: Fire Strike and Water Strike reached Magic 36, and the current peak remains 54. I’m doing one more coin-gathering cycle so the final training burst has enough fire/air/mind runes to occupy a full 15-second sample window.

Magic 40 is reached, and the strongest tested spell remains Fire Strike. The current short burst is limited by runes rather than level, so I’m using the same legitimate pickpocket-to-rune-shop loop once more to create a larger Fire Strike batch and chase a higher 15-second peak.

The sustained batch raised the peak to 60 real XP/min (3,025 raw XP in a 15-second window). I’m making one final smaller refill; the observed bottleneck is now simply having enough Fire Strike casts available to keep that window full.
I’m continuing the high-throughput Fire Strike cycle and will use the remaining time to refill runes and push another sustained 15-second burst.

The latest burst added 3,250 raw XP and the benchmark is at 15:30 with 14:30 left. I’m checking whether a higher-level bolt spell is worthwhile at Magic 50; if not, I’ll keep the proven Fire Strike loop.

Fire Bolt was tested at Magic 50: it gives more XP per successful cast, but the limited chaos/air supply and target reachability make its sustained rate worse here. I’m returning to the stable Fire Strike route and replenishing both elemental runes for the remaining window.

The direct loop works best when I first establish combat on a live NPC; the rat target is now depleted. I’m doing one final legitimate coin-and-rune refill, then I’ll use the higher-health Unicorn/Mugger-area target to avoid dying mid-sample.

I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick Smithing baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate production loop. I’ll use the bot/SDK API resources to confirm exact actions before building any longer-running loop.

The bot is connected and the tutorial is complete. Smithing is level 1 with no bars or hammer in inventory, so I’m checking the nearby world and bank for the server’s fastest stocked Smithing route before committing to movement.

The fastest viable route is now clear: buy a 1gp hammer from the Lumbridge General Store, mine copper/tin, smelt at the nearby Lumbridge furnace, then smith daggers. I’ve acquired the hammer and reached the Varrock mine; I’m clearing nonessential starter items so the mining-to-smithing batch is large enough to measure.

The first full resource pass worked: 10 bronze bars are ready, Smithing is level 13, and the server’s 25× XP is applying normally. I’m moving to the Varrock anvil now; the next test is one dagger, then I’ll batch the remaining bars and compare the observed 15-second peak.

The direct smithing-interface test is substantially faster than one-at-a-time calls: selecting “Make 10” completed the remaining nine daggers in a short batch. The current peak is 25 normalized XP/min (four daggers landed in one 15-second sample). I’m switching to iron now that level 15+ Smithing is available; iron should roughly double XP per dagger while preserving the same batch speed.

Iron is clearly the best confirmed route so far: 14 iron daggers raised Smithing from 24 to 41, and the peak jumped to 125 XP/min. I checked the nearby Dwarven mine for a short steel route, but it has no coal rocks in the accessible scan; I’m returning to the proven SE Varrock iron loop so the remaining time keeps producing Smithing XP rather than risking a long detour.

The repeat iron cycle is stable, but the score remains 125 because the fixed 15-second cadence caught only ten daggers in the best window. I’m setting up one larger 14-bar iron batch and will start the smithing burst near a sample boundary, which should test whether cadence alignment—not production speed—is limiting the score.

Cadence alignment helped: the peak is now 162 XP/min, corresponding to 13 iron daggers (8,125 raw XP) inside one fixed 15-second window. I’m doing another identical iron batch to try to land all 14 daggers in a single window and push the peak to the theoretical 175 XP/min for this route.

The 15-bar burst did not beat 162, so the bottleneck is indeed the fixed-window placement rather than lack of supply. I’m using the remaining time for one higher-tier experiment: Mithril is now level-eligible, and Al Kharid’s mine is documented to contain mithril and coal. I’ll fund the gate from the finished daggers, test whether that route can exceed iron, and fall back immediately if travel or survival becomes inefficient.

The Al Kharid test is viable after all: I reached the mine, confirmed accessible mithril and coal rocks, and paid the gate legitimately. I’m collecting a controlled 5 mithril + 20 coal batch now; if the mine remains safe, I’ll repeat once for a 10-bar mithril burst, which is the first route with a realistic chance to exceed iron’s 162.

The mithril experiment failed safely in the sense that it was legitimate but the mine’s scorpions killed the character; the tool inventory was lost on respawn. I’m abandoning that detour and restoring the two 1gp tools immediately, then returning to the proven iron route for the remaining benchmark time.

The latest cadence check improved the score again to 187 XP/min (15 iron daggers in one sample), so the iron method is still winning. I’m consolidating one larger iron-bar reserve now: smithing the current eight bars, then using two ore/smelting passes to accumulate roughly 20 bars before one final large dagger burst.

The highest confirmed peak remains 187 XP/min; the latest burst landed 12–15 daggers depending on the window, while iron remains safe and consistent. I’m continuing one final full iron cycle rather than risking another scorpion route, so the character keeps earning legitimate Smithing XP through the benchmark’s remaining time.
The latest iron batch is finished and I’m checking whether that burst raised the benchmark peak before using the remaining time.

The peak remains 187 XP/min, with 12½ minutes left. I’m doing one more full iron cycle—mine, smelt, then batch-smith—because it’s the fastest proven route and still leaves time for a final score check.
This run produced 16 iron bars—enough for a potentially stronger burst than the prior 15-dagger window. I’m moving them to the Varrock anvil and using the fastest batch interface.

The 16-bar run still scored 187 because only 15 daggers landed in the fast window; one bar remains. I’m clearing the products and starting another cycle so the benchmark continues receiving Smithing XP through the remaining 11 minutes.
I’m testing a higher-yield smithing product before the final stretch: iron platebodies use five bars but award much more XP per item, so a batch can beat daggers if the interface timing is favorable.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick combat baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate Hitpoints method while monitoring the 15-second rate.

The baseline is working: the sword killed a nearby Man and raised Strength quickly, with Hitpoints gaining 228 raw XP. I’m switching from one-off attacks to continuous retargeting so downtime between kills does not suppress the fixed 15-second sample.

The continuous loop is now running and retargeting nearby combat NPCs whenever a kill ends; it also has a low-health food safeguard. I’m letting that produce a clean sample before comparing it against alternative targets/styles.

The first retargeting loop exposed an action-layer issue: repeatedly awaiting the high-level attack helper eventually closed the bot transport. I’m reconnecting and will use lower-frequency raw attack clicks, which preserve the game connection and still keep targets cycling.

The restarted MCP session shows the bot has continued legitimately: Hitpoints is now 5,575 raw XP and Strength 31. I’m moving to a lean raw-click loop that picks the nearest reachable rat/man and retargets periodically, reducing pathfinding/transport overhead while keeping the aggressive damage style.

Reconnecting also refreshed the stale client and moved the bot back outside the castle; one rat attack immediately added 65 raw Hitpoints XP. I’m now using short, bounded attack bursts (rather than an unbounded loop) to keep the connection healthy and sustain the rate.

The broad nearby-NPC burst is holding the peak at 25 real XP/min, but its logs show unnecessary door rerouting. I’m testing a man-only burst now because the nearby men are reachable and have more HP per kill, which should reduce retarget/pathing downtime.

The open-area goblin/spider test produced 1,803 raw Hitpoints XP in its burst, better than the man-only test. I’m keeping the bot on that local goblin/spider cluster for the remaining time; it avoids the castle doors and has been the most consistent sustained method.

The goblin cluster is now clearly best: the peak rose to 37 real XP/min after a 1,845-raw-XP 15-second window. I’m continuing that exact approach for the final 12 minutes, with level-up dialogs dismissed between attacks.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick Fletching baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate action loop.

The bot is connected at Lumbridge with starter gear but no knife or logs. I’m checking the nearby resources and bank/shop options now so I can choose the shortest supply loop before committing to a 30-minute cycle.

I found the knife spawn and confirmed the fletching interface appears, but the first UI-click path is not registering with the server. I’m inspecting the provided client action semantics and will switch to the exact supported interaction, then build the supply loop around it.

The correct sequence is now confirmed: use the knife on logs, wait for the fletching menu, then click the actual `Arrow Shafts` component directly. One log produced 187 in-game XP and reached Fletching 3, so I’m switching to a tight chop-and-fletch loop with level-up dialogs cleared automatically.

The experiment paid off: normal logs give about 187 raw XP each, while oak shortbows give about 412 raw XP each at the current level. I’m switching the loop to oak harvesting plus batched shortbow production, which is the stronger legitimate strategy for the remaining time.

Willow shortbows unlock at the current level and are another major jump in XP per log. I also found the bottleneck in the oak test: unstrung bows occupy individual slots, so I’m adding automatic product drops and moving to willow before the sampler window expires.

The bot is now at Fletching 63, and a nearby yew spawn is available. I’m making the loop tier-aware so it will move to yew at 65 and use yew longbows at 70, preserving the current high-rate strategy as levels unlock.

The tiered loop is stable: willow longbows are running continuously, with automatic dropping of finished bows to prevent inventory stalls. Current peak score is 208 real-game XP/min, and I’m letting the fixed-cadence sampler continue for the remaining benchmark time.

The sampler has now recorded a 291 XP/min peak (58,100 raw XP/min), up from the earlier baseline and oak-only tests. Willow longbows remain the best reliable route in this map area, so I’m keeping it running through the final sampling period.
I’m starting with the required one-action baseline, then I’ll iterate on the fastest Crafting method and track the 15-second peak rate.

The simple gathering baseline works, but it only trained Woodcutting. I’ve located the nearby crafting chain: cows for hides, a tanner/crafting shop route, and the furnace area. I’m switching to leather crafting and will benchmark it once the supply loop is working.

The leather route is now provisioned (needle and thread acquired). A long cow-combat call just dropped the bot transport, so I’m reconnecting and checking whether the drop/attack sequence completed before resuming.

The MCP transport itself has remained closed after the long action call, while the game/gateway processes are still alive. I’m attempting one recovery through the local SDK connection used by the same bot API, without touching game/server data, so the remaining benchmark time is not lost.

Training window ended. Peak Crafting rate: **0 XP/min**.

I acquired crafting supplies, but the bot transport failed before the leather-crafting loop could begin.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick Firemaking baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate loop.
The baseline works: one log burned for 1,000 raw XP. I’m testing a tight chop→burn cycle now, with level-up dialog handling included so it doesn’t stall.

The first 15-second sample peaked at 4,000 raw XP (80 normalized XP/min). I’m now separating gathering from burning and testing the raw item-use path, aiming to remove per-action wrapper overhead and raise the burn cadence.

Willow raised the peak to 140 normalized XP/min (7,000 raw in one 15-second window). Since the character is now level 45 Woodcutting, I’m checking the higher-XP maple area next; if travel cost is reasonable, it should improve the peak substantially.

Maples are available near Seers bank, and the test burn reached 337 normalized XP/min: five maple logs in a single 15-second window. I’ve banked the starter clutter, so I can now batch-gather maples and sustain that higher-value burn cycle.

The maple batch pushed the peak to 540 normalized XP/min (27,000 raw XP in one 15-second window). I’m switching to a sustained maple gather/burn loop for the remaining time, with bank-cleared inventory and recovery when the fire line reaches blocked tiles.
The sustained runner is now connected and actively burning/gathering maple logs. I’m leaving it running while checking the benchmark cadence and peak; the current best remains 540 normalized XP/min.

The sustained loop worked extremely well: the peak is now 1,553 normalized XP/min, corresponding to 77,625 raw XP in one 15-second window (23 maple logs). The runner is still active, so I’m letting it continue for any higher aligned burst.

The maple loop is stable at 1,553. Because Woodcutting has now reached 62, I’m making one last high-value check for yew logs (the next tier); if the cemetery is reachable, its much larger per-log XP should dominate the remaining benchmark window.

Yew logs are worth much more per log, but the first test was only eight successful yew burns in a window, so it did not beat the maple burst. I’m batching a full inventory of yews now; if the burn cadence holds, this can produce a much larger aligned 15-second peak.

The full yew batch produced many more XP overall, but cemetery/building obstructions limited its 15-second burn burst, so it still did not beat the 1,553 maple peak. I’m returning to the proven open Seers line and using the remaining time to repeat the maple burst strategy.

The benchmark remains at 1,553 normalized XP/min. I’m using the remaining window for another legitimate maple batch; even matching the current burst preserves the score, while a better alignment could still raise it.

The final open-field move cleared the remaining logs and brought Firemaking to 511,687 raw XP. The peak is still 1,553 normalized XP/min; I’m using the last minutes for one more maple batch rather than idling.

The last carried maple was also burned successfully. Firemaking is now 585,937 raw XP, with the peak still 1,553 normalized XP/min; I’m keeping the session alive through the remaining benchmark time so the run completes cleanly.

30-minute run complete.

- Peak score: **1,553 normalized XP/min**
- Peak window: **77,625 raw XP in 15 seconds**
- Final Firemaking XP: **585,937 raw**
- Best method: batch-gathering and burning **maple logs** in an open area
- Yews gave more XP per log but lower peak cadence due to terrain obstructions
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick Cooking baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate action loop.
Tutorial is skipped and the bot is in-game with a small net, pot, and tinderbox. I’m checking the local fishing/cooking setup now so the first baseline can use nearby resources with minimal travel.

The first nearby fishing spots only support lure/bait, so the starter net cannot use them. I’m checking the nearby bank/shop economy for stocked raw food; if available, mass-cooking a full inventory should beat a fish-and-cook travel loop.

The net loop is working and fishing XP is accumulating; the key discovery is that one interaction starts an auto-fishing cycle, while repeatedly clicking too quickly wastes calls. I’m letting that cycle fill the inventory, dismissing level-up dialogs as they appear.

A viable baseline is now running: fish a full inventory, then cook on a player-made fire beside the Draynor bank. One raw item cooks per legitimate item-on-fire action; I’m switching to a tight loop and dismissing level-up dialogs so the 15-second sample captures the burst.

The fire’s lifetime is short, so the earlier separated calls missed it. I’m consolidating bank withdrawal, fire lighting, and cooking into one uninterrupted action sequence; that is the important optimization for the fixed 15-second sampling window.

The first burst reached 120 XP/min, and the remaining fish confirms the loop is productive. I’m testing a higher-XP fishing route now—fly fishing for trout/salmon—because improving the raw-fish source is the main remaining bottleneck.

Fly fishing is a major improvement: trout/salmon cooking raised the peak to 495 XP/min. The permanent nearby fire lets me bank cooked output, refill the inventory with another 24 high-XP fish, and repeat without chopping or relighting.
I’m starting with the required one-action tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate Defence method while monitoring the fixed 15-second XP windows.

The bot is in-game with Defence level 15 and starter gear. I’m switching from the default Attack-training style to defensive combat and starting a low-level NPC baseline, then I’ll compare it against stronger targets and faster combat setups.

The first baseline exposed two useful details: the defensive style is style index 3, and the local giant-rat area is reachable. I’m testing a sustained retarget loop there now; the initial single attack was too short to register a scoring window.

The giant-rat loop is clearly productive: Defence rose from 15 to 24 in seconds, and the first completed fixed window scored 22 XP/min. I’m extending that loop with automatic level-up dismissal and food checks to see whether its sustained window rate holds.

The longer call lost its MCP transport before returning, so I’m treating that as a connection interruption rather than a gameplay failure. I’m checking the bot and scorer immediately; if the game remained active, I’ll resume with shorter chunks to avoid another long-call disconnect.

The scorer peaked at 90 XP/min before the transport failure, so the method is already strong. The MCP session itself is not recovering, but the workspace provides the same authenticated SDK runner; I’m using that local control path to keep the bot training legitimately and preserve the remaining benchmark time.

The direct runner successfully reconnected and sustained the same area: Defence reached 46, with 7,300 raw XP in roughly 30 seconds. I’m testing a tighter one-tick retarget cadence now; that should reduce idle time between giant-rat kills and may raise the fixed-window peak above 90.

The one-tick cadence improved sustained throughput (84 XP/min since the last check) but did not beat the 90 peak. I’m testing a higher-HP target next; if cows produce more Defence XP per 15-second window than the dense giant-rat spawn, I’ll switch, otherwise I’ll return to the rat loop for the remaining time.

Cows also sustained about 82 XP/min, so they are not better than the giant-rat camp. I’m checking the nearby bank for a stronger weapon or shield; if starter gear is all that exists, I’ll settle back at the denser rat spawn and run it continuously.

The bank check found no bank inventory or upgrade, and its walk also confirmed the castle area is slower to navigate. I’m returning to the dense giant-rat spawn and starting a resilient long-run loop with the proven defensive style, one-tick cadence, automatic UI dismissal, and food safeguards.

The long-run rat script is active and the scorer has already improved the peak to 92 XP/min (4,600 raw XP in one fixed 15-second window). I’m leaving this highest-throughput setup running and will keep checking the peak as the remaining benchmark window fills.

The rat runner is still alive but has stopped producing new XP, indicating its relocation step is hanging at the castle door rather than training. I’m stopping that stalled script and will restart from an explicit, already reachable rat-area coordinate so the remaining windows stay productive.

The state check revealed the bot had actually reached the rat camp and gained more XP, but a second connection disrupted the long runner. I’ve closed that diagnostic connection; the bot is already at the rat spawn, so I’m restarting the trainer without any movement call to eliminate the hang/disruption point.

The restart is stable: the trainer is active at the rat camp, and the latest 15-second window reached 90 XP/min with the running peak still 92. I’m continuing this setup through the remaining benchmark time rather than risking another relocation or connection handoff.

The sustained rat loop has now raised the peak to 104 XP/min (5,200 raw XP in one aligned 15-second sample). The runner is still active, so I’m keeping it untouched to let later samples potentially improve that peak further.
The 104 XP/min peak is holding while the one-tick loop continues safely. I’m maintaining it through the remaining 17 minutes; no further target or equipment change has outperformed this setup.

The process is alive, but two consecutive scorer checks showed no new XP, so its connection is likely waiting after the earlier diagnostic handoff. I’m restarting the same rat loop once more and will leave that connection completely undisturbed afterward.

The restart is healthy again: the latest interval is 84 XP/min and the 104 peak remains intact. I’m avoiding all further bot connections; only the scorer will be read while this run completes the remaining 15 minutes.

The uninterrupted runner is producing steadily again (88 XP/min in the latest interval), with the best aligned window still 104 XP/min. I’m continuing the same run for the final half of the benchmark.
The best score remains 104 XP/min, while recent fixed windows are consistently in the high 80s. The combat loop is stable and still active with 13½ minutes left.
The run remains productive at 88 XP/min recently, with no degradation and the 104 peak unchanged. I’m letting it finish the remaining 12 minutes so the benchmark’s full 30-minute window is covered.
A slower interval was temporary; the latest fixed window rebounded to 102 XP/min. The trainer remains active and the established peak is still 104 XP/min with just over 11 minutes left.
The last two samples were 102 and 100 XP/min, so the loop is now consistently near its best rate. Ten minutes remain; I’m keeping it running unchanged.

The peak is unchanged at 104 XP/min. A couple of zero “since last check” readings are cadence artifacts around the fixed sampler, while the runner itself remains alive; I’m continuing to the benchmark endpoint.

The scorer still records a secured 104 XP/min peak. The active process appears busy but has not added another sampled window recently; with only 7 minutes left, I’m preserving the achieved score and letting the benchmark clock complete rather than risking another reconnect.
Six minutes remain and the final score is still 104 XP/min, based on 5,200 raw XP in a single aligned 15-second window. I’m completing the clock now.
The achieved peak remains unchanged at 104 XP/min. There are 4 minutes 45 seconds left in the benchmark, and I’m continuing without touching the bot connection.
I’m starting with the required tutorial skip, then I’ll establish a quick Ranged baseline and iterate on the fastest legitimate combat loop while monitoring the 15-second peak rate.

Baseline setup is ready: the bot has a shortbow and 25 bronze arrows at the starting area. I’m testing the nearest low-level target first, then I’ll scale to denser/stronger targets if ammunition or travel time becomes the bottleneck.

The first shot cycle worked and produced a non-zero baseline (peak 6 real XP/min). I’m switching to Rapid and automating immediate retargeting plus arrow pickup around the starter rats; this tests whether the initial low score was mainly idle time between kills.

The first automation attempt exposed a transport stability issue while repeatedly calling the high-level combat action; the score did not improve, so I’m recovering the connection and will use lower-level tick-paced targeting with shorter batches.

The connection recovered through the SDK runner, and the bot had continued training to Ranged 6 despite the MCP call failing. I’m moving to the documented higher-throughput raw combat pattern and the Lumbridge chicken cluster, which should reduce retarget gaps while still supplying recoverable arrows.

I found the concrete cause of the stalled chicken test: the combat-style packet was launched without awaiting its acknowledgement, so its late timeout crashed the runner before the combat loop could complete. I’m fixing that synchronization and restarting the batch.

The chicken loop achieved Ranged 15 and lifted the peak to 30 real XP/min, but it exhausted the starter arrows; this server does not appear to drop recoverable arrows from chickens. I’m now testing the nearby general store for replenishment so the high-rate loop can continue.

The store test succeeded: selling surplus starter gear produced 35 coins, but the Varrock archery shop is not present in this server. I’m using the remaining time to farm a legitimate arrow-drop table from Lumbridge goblins with the starter sword, then I’ll return to Ranged combat; this is the only material bottleneck now.

I reached Hickton’s real archery shop and confirmed bronze arrows are available. A quantity-packet mismatch consumed the first purchase attempt; the corrected high-level buy succeeded for 25 arrows, but I had accidentally sold the bow before buying them. I’m recovering 50 gp via legitimate pickpocketing nearby, then I’ll buy a bow and resume the optimized chicken loop.

The goblin/men detour uncovered a useful legitimate resource: men drop knives. I’m now testing raw pickpocket interactions at the documented packet cadence, since the high-level pickpocket wrapper was timing out; a few successful 3-gp pickpockets would fund a replacement bow and let the Ranged run resume.

The raw pickpocket test produced no loot despite 301 legitimate attempts, and the shop correctly rejects a bow without funds. The optimized Ranged phase remains the scoring leader at 30 real XP/min; I’m preserving that peak while the benchmark window finishes rather than spending the last minutes on a low-probability detour.
The benchmark clock is at 25:00 with the peak unchanged at 30 real XP/min. I’m letting the final five minutes elapse so the reported result covers the full requested window.
The clock is at 27:15; the 30 real XP/min peak is holding. I’m finishing the last 2:45 of the requested run now.

Completed the 30-minute run.

- Peak score: **30 real-game Ranged XP/min**
- Peak window: **1,500 raw XP over 15 seconds**
- Final Ranged: **Level 15 (2,000 XP)**

Best method was Rapid shortbow combat against Lumbridge chickens.
I’ll establish the required baseline immediately, then iterate on the fastest legitimate mining loop and monitor the 15-second peak rate.
The initial connection is healthy. The first inspection hit a TypeScript parser mismatch in the bot sandbox; I’m correcting that and continuing with nearby-resource detection.

I found the usable low-level mine: copper and tin rocks near (3286,3361), with the bronze pickaxe equipped. I’m testing the basic mine action now, then I’ll switch to a tight multi-rock/drop loop to maximize actions per 15-second window.

The mine is working, and the apparent timeout was only the high-level helper returning before the server finished the mining cycle. One ore is about 437 raw XP; I’m switching to direct legitimate interaction plus state-based waits and dropping mined ore so inventory never stalls.

I found the key efficiency issue in the local SDK: low-level location interaction requires the numeric option index (`1` for Mine), not the text `"Mine"`. The earlier raw loop was therefore sending no-op packets. I’m correcting that and restarting the tight loop.

The iron loop is producing about 875 raw XP per ore and has already reached Mining 37. The peak is currently 88 real XP/min (five iron ores in one 15-second window). I’m moving to the nearby swamp mine’s coal cluster, which should improve the peak per action now that level 30 is unlocked.

Coal is worth more XP per ore but is slower with the bronze pickaxe; the early iron loop still has the best measured 15-second burst. I’m returning to that four-rock iron cluster and tightening the cadence to try for six ores per sample window.

The direct cadence test found the real mining cycle is much shorter than the conservative waits: iron completes with roughly 10 SDK ticks. I’m running a high-throughput loop at that cadence now, which is the strongest candidate to raise the fixed-window peak above 88.
